Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 4-2y+3z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 3}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070533/assets/6e48e66eb003be316573e5b44948fcbce43b07e78fea97a7865ecf5eb4b4404a.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le x\le 4-2y+3z}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4-2y+3z}\frac{yz}{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4-2y+3z}\frac{yz}{2}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{4-2y+3z}\frac{yz}{2}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{yz}{2}[x]_{x=0}^{x=4-2y+3z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{yz}{2}(4-2y+3z)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(4yz-2{y}^{2}z+3y{z}^{2})\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(4yz-2{y}^{2}z+3y{z}^{2})\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(4yz-2{y}^{2}z+3y{z}^{2})\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}{[2y{z}^{2}-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+y{z}^{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(18y-9{y}^{2}+27y)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(45y-9{y}^{2})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(45y-9{y}^{2})\,dy & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{45}{2}{y}^{2}-3{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(90-24)-0 \\  & =33.\end{aligned}
$$
